purpose: Map only: the eye pass as a unit, for single-pass stereo. OBVR renders a dual-pass frame by calling OSGlobals::RenderScene 0x0040C830 twice through its hook, with the camera moved between the two calls (../OBVR/src/render/SceneRenderHook.cpp; its CullingSync replays the first eye's cull results in the second, its ShadowShareHook keeps the first eye's actor shadow maps). Measured on the fixed Walkers scene (knowledge/culling-and-draw-setup.md, 'Round two'): the two eye passes hold 4.98 of the frame's 5.36 ms of draw work - per partition the shader slots 13/15/14 take 2.85 ms for both eyes, the device draws with the palette build about 2.1 ms, the accumulator's lists 0.44 ms. A single pass that culls and sets up once and draws every partition twice (left viewport, right viewport) would keep the draws and save the second eye's setup and lists: about 1.6 ms a frame, the largest lever left. The slice must give the contract of one eye pass: which engine state is eye-dependent (the view and projection the renderer builds from the camera, the viewport, the render target, the culling planes, the light constants?), where it is set, and where in the per-partition draw a second draw with the other eye's state can be inserted (the instructions between the last setup and the DrawIndexedPrimitive, and what has to be re-set between the two draws). No rebuild in this run.
